relationships.subject: Caffeine
relationships.evidence_quote: Caffeine has primarily been studied for its pain-relieving effects through the competitive inhibition of adenosine receptors (ARs)

relationships.subject: Caffeine
relationships.evidence_quote: downregulating cyclooxygenase-2(COX-2), antagonizing the adenosine receptor

relationships.subject: Caffeine
relationships.evidence_quote: caffeine is theorized to act as an antagonist of TRPA1 channels

relationships.subject: Caffeine
relationships.evidence_quote: caffeine is theorized to have an agonistic effect on TRPV1 channels, leading to eventual receptor desensitization and downregulation

relationships.subject: Bradykinin
relationships.evidence_quote: TRPA1 has been shown to be modulated by proalgesic and proinflammatory agents, such as bradykinin activating phospholipase C, contributing to excitation and sensitization of nociceptive neurons

key_findings: Review: caffeine may regulate TRPV1 (agonism/desensitization) and TRPA1 (antagonism), but direct molecular evidence is scarce.
Caffeine analgesia is mainly via adenosine receptor antagonism and possibly COX-2 downregulation.
